title: Require Categorical Service Context Boundaries
forbids: a root base without the deps, scope, config, invocation, and provided lanes; root middleware not authored from base.middleware or any root middleware runtime export other than middleware; a root middleware import outside impl.ts, without a semantic alias, or not attached to the exported service lineage; a noncanonical module middleware leaf or one authored from neither base.middleware nor an unconfigured router descendant rooted at the owning impl.<module>; a module middleware index without only documented semantic aliases to native decorated middleware leaves; module.ts or a router leaf bypassing that middleware index or leaving an imported catalog value unattached from its exported native chain; explicit .use type arguments in implementation, module, or operation leaves; a module without inferred inline terminal curation, a block curation whose direct terminal return is not its sole next call, or one that renames context/next, passes or spreads context, projects whole raw lanes through dot or bracket access, or emits a raw-lane output key; or an operation leaf that reopens a raw context lane through property, bracket, or destructuring access
why: One base declaration establishes explicit ownership and lifetime lanes. A native base author exists only when context-authored middleware needs it. Policy attachment follows ownership: module-wide at module.ts, reusable group policy across a deliberate grouped router leaf, and exact-operation policy inline on the procedure. Reusable validated-input policy also remains procedure-attached because native oRPC records that attachment after the procedure schema, while router middleware runs before procedure input validation. Grit proves visible roots, destinations, and catalog attachment; TypeScript proves the native router/procedure authoring distinction; behavior proof owns validation order; and review proves semantic reuse, matching group ownership, and the absence of helpers, decorators, or extracted types that simulate a missing oRPC authoring surface. Terminal module curation leaves handlers with only their operation vocabulary.
remediate: Declare all five Context lanes in base.ts. Export base = os.$context<Context>() only when context-authored middleware consumes it. Give every service-root middleware leaf a direct simple kebab-case filename and exactly one documented runtime export named middleware from base.middleware(...); import it by semantic alias in impl.ts, attach it to the service lineage, and do not create a root barrel. Give every module middleware leaf a simple kebab-case filename and export one documented context middleware from base.middleware(...) or reusable policy from an unconfigured router descendant rooted at impl.<lowerCamelModule>. Keep module middleware/index.ts to documented semantic re-exports of those native decorated middleware values. Import module-wide middleware into module.ts only through ./middleware and attach each imported name there. Import reusable group policy into its deliberate grouped router leaf through ../middleware and visibly attach it on the exported native chain. A reusable validated-input policy may instead attach through the same catalog at each native procedure .use(...) so oRPC runs it after that procedure's input schema. Router authorship separately owns filename-to-terminal-operation and filename-to-group-root alignment. Keep truly operation-only policy inline; review owns whether a named policy is genuinely reused and whether its authoring descendant owns the same scope. Do not simulate a procedure middleware author with a helper, decorator, or extracted procedure type. Keep router indexes and direct, deep, alias, sibling, and arbitrary-parent middleware routes closed. End module.ts with an inferred inline curation whose context/next names stay stable, whose block form calls next exactly once through the direct terminal return, and whose output selects explicit members without passing, spreading, renaming, or emitting whole raw lanes.
message: Service context must descend through the native five-lane capability funnel.
